definition: A training technique that averages model weights collected across multiple points along the training trajectory, typically improving generalization compared to using the final checkpoint alone.
details: SWA leverages the observation that averaging weights from different points in training (particularly with a modified learning rate schedule) often finds flatter, better-generalizing regions of the loss landscape than a single final checkpoint.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Stochastic Weight Averaging.

citation.title: Averaging Weights Leads to Wider Optima and Better Generalization
